# @xano-sdk/auth

> A [Xano SDK](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@xano/sdk) package implementing
> Xano's quick-start authentication (`auth/signup`, `auth/login`, `auth/me`, plus
> the `user`, `account`, and `event_log` tables and an event-log function),
> recreated as typed Xano SDK defs you register into a workspace and version
> behind npm. It is also the **reference Xano SDK extension package**.
> It is **authentication, not authorization**: it ships no permission checks
> and no route guards, so it is not the RBAC answer.

A Xano SDK extension package exports plain, typed def objects (the factories
`table()`, `query()`, `defineFunction()`, `apiGroup()` are pure identity
functions). The *consumer's* `Xano` instance does all registration and encoding
via `export()`. This package pins no guids, and no canonical unless you pass one
to `registerAuth` — otherwise identity comes from the consuming project's
`xano.lock`, or falls back to `md5("<kind>:<name>")`.

## Install

```bash
npm install @xano-sdk/auth @xano/sdk
```

`@xano/sdk` is a `>=1.0.0 <2.0.0` peer dependency — install the current stable
release. Built and tested against 1.0.0. The golden-bundle test in this package
is the peer-drift tripwire: if an SDK upgrade changes encoding, it fails here
before consumers are affected (for the installed version — the rest of the range
is declared, not CI-verified).

The floor is the highest of three requirements: the golden bundle, which the
committed fixture matches from the floor up; the `guard.role` the role-check
guidance below relies on; and the `db.get` miss-to-null that `auth/me`'s derived
response type needs. The ceiling is the SDK's next major, since any major may
change what the defs encode to. Below the floor is unsupported, and a
golden-bundle failure anywhere else is real drift.

## Quickstart

`npx xanosdk init <dir> --marketplace @xano-sdk/auth` scaffolds a project with the
registration below already in `xano/index.ts`. In an existing project, `npx xanosdk
marketplace install @xano-sdk/auth` installs the package and prints the registration
lines; add them by hand:

```ts
// xano/index.ts
import { workspace } from "@xano/sdk";
import { registerAuth } from "@xano-sdk/auth";

// Pin `canonical` to make getPath() resolve client-side with no lock file;
// omit the options object to leave the canonical to the consumer's xano.lock.
export default registerAuth(workspace("my-app"), { canonical: "authn" });
```

```bash
npx xanosdk deploy                                 # → disposable backend + URL (after `npx xanosdk login`)
npx xanosdk export xano/index.ts -o bundle.json    # → importable workspace bundle
```

## Exports

- `registerAuth(xano, opts?)` — one-call install of the full set; returns the
  instance for chaining. Idempotency-guarded (throws on a second call per
  instance). `opts.canonical` pins the Authentication group's URL segment (see
  the getPath note below); omit it to leave identity to the consumer's lock.
  `opts.history` sets the group's request-history capture and **defaults to
  `false`** (see the constraint below); pass `true`, a positive capture depth,
  or `"all"` to opt in.
- Tables: `userTable` (auth table), `accountTable`, `eventLogTable`
- Function: `createEventLogFn`
- API: `authenticationGroup`, `signupQuery`, `loginQuery`, `meQuery`
- Types (erase at compile time — `import type` costs no bundle bytes):
  `User`, `PublicUser`, `Account`, `EventLog`, `AuthTokenResponse`,
  `RegisterAuthOptions`
- `PUBLIC_USER_FIELDS` — the runtime array `auth/me` selects; `PublicUser` is
  `Pick<User, typeof PUBLIC_USER_FIELDS[number]>`, so the two cannot drift.

## Calling the endpoints from a typed client

Every query carries its own route and payload types, so a frontend reuses the
def instead of re-typing URLs and bodies. Request types are derived; all three
responses are fully resolved — no `unknown` — `me` by derivation, `signup` and
`login` by a hand-declared `responseShape`:

```ts
// Evaluating the module that calls registerAuth is what pins the canonical;
// without it the bare getPath() below throws. Or use getPath({ canonical }).
import "./xano/index.js";
import { loginQuery, meQuery, type AuthTokenResponse } from "@xano-sdk/auth";
import type { InferInput, InferResponse } from "@xano/sdk";

type LoginBody = InferInput<typeof loginQuery>;      // { email?: string; password?: string }
type LoginOut  = InferResponse<typeof loginQuery>;   // AuthTokenResponse
type MeOut     = InferResponse<typeof meQuery>;      // PublicUser | null

const BASE = "https://your-instance.xano.io";

const res = await fetch(BASE + loginQuery.getPath(), {
  method: loginQuery.verb,                            // "POST"
  headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
  body: JSON.stringify({ email, password } satisfies LoginBody),
});
const { authToken }: LoginOut = await res.json();
```

`signup`/`login` declare `responseShape: AuthTokenResponse` because the token is
minted by a statement (opaque to the static walk); a declared shape overrides
derivation and is not cross-checked against the stack, so those two are a
hand-maintained contract. `meQuery` declares **nothing** — the SDK derives
`PublicUser | null` from its stack, narrowing the `db.get` to the columns in
`PUBLIC_USER_FIELDS` and carrying that statement's miss-to-null. The `| null` is
the faithful-port quirk below surfacing in the type, not an oversight: callers
are forced to handle a token whose user row is gone. Do not add a
`responseShape` to `meQuery` — it would only let the declaration drift from the
`output` list.

**`getPath()` needs a canonical.** It builds `/api:<canonical>/<name>`, and by
default this package pins none (identity is the consumer's lock). A canonical
can't be minted on demand — it must be unique per instance — so a **bare
`getPath()` throws** unless one is supplied. Preferred: pin it at registration,
`registerAuth(workspace("my-app"), { canonical: "authn" })`, which makes the
deployed path and the client-derived path one value and needs no lock in the
browser (an in-code canonical beats the lock; it must match `[A-Za-z0-9_-]+`,
and because the group def is process-wide, once pinned every later
`registerAuth` must pass the same value — a different value *or* an omitted one
throws, rather than retargeting or being silently inherited by a workspace
registered earlier. Uniqueness across the instance's API groups is the caller's
responsibility; a collision surfaces at Xano import). Otherwise pass it per call,
`getPath({ canonical })`, or seed the lock at startup with
`seedLockOverrides(readLockFile("./xano.lock"))` BEFORE importing any def module
(defs bake references at import time, so seeding later is a silent no-op) —
`readLockFile` comes from the Node-only `@xano/sdk/node` entry. `xanosdk export
<entry>` and `xanosdk deploy` write `xano.lock` beside the entry by default, so the
first run mints and freezes the canonical; commit the lock.

**In a browser bundle, generate routes instead of importing defs.** Importing any
def pulls in the SDK runtime (~267 kB minified / ~65 kB gzipped for the first
def). `npx xanosdk routes xano/index.ts --emit xano/routes.gen.ts` writes the same
verbs and paths as plain data that imports nothing, still compile-checked; keep
the defs for `import type` only.

Cherry-pick individual defs instead of `registerAuth` for granular control; keep
each def's dependencies together (queries need `userTable`; `createEventLogFn`
needs `eventLogTable`). Never register a def twice.

## Constraints for agents (read before using)

- **Authentication, not authorization — this is not the RBAC answer.** The
  package mints and verifies tokens; it ships no permission checks and no route
  guards. `userTable` carries a `role` enum (`admin` | `member`, set to
  `"member"` on signup) and `auth/me` returns it, but nothing here enforces it,
  and `create_auth_token` is called with empty `extras`, so the role is **not**
  on the token — `auth("role")` resolves to nothing. Enforce roles with the
  SDK's `guard.role`: in a query whose `auth` is `userTable`, spread
  `...guard.role(userTable, "admin")` into the stack. It loads the caller's row by
  `auth("id")`, rejects a missing row (401), then checks `role` (403). Do not
  hand-roll a `db.get` + `precondition` on `caller.role`: drilling into a missing
  row is a 500, not a denial. Do not adopt this package expecting authorization
  to come with it.
- **`userTable` is this package's auth table** (`auth: true`), and `auth/me`
  names it directly (the SDK binds a query's `auth` to a table def, not `true`). A
  consumer may register their own additional `auth: true` table; these endpoints
  still authenticate against `user`.
- **Call `registerAuth` at most once per `Xano` instance** — it throws otherwise.
- **Request history is OFF by default**, unlike the engine (whose queries
  inherit it ON). History records the request body, so an inheriting
  `auth/signup`/`auth/login` would store the plaintext password and the minted
  24h non-revokable token. `registerAuth` sets it `false` on the Authentication
  group and the three queries inherit that. Opt back in for local debugging with
  `registerAuth(xano, { history: true | <depth> | "all" })`. Process-wide, like
  `canonical`: a later call that would change it throws. Do not tell a user to
  mutate `authenticationGroup.history` — it is only needed on the cherry-pick
  path, and a value disagreeing with the `registerAuth` call is an error.
- **This is a close port of Xano's quick-start template**; its quirks are
  preserved on purpose, except the two credential leaks fixed in
  [xanots/sdk#10](https://github.com/xanots/sdk/issues/10) (request history
  above, and `event_log.metadata` below). Notably:
  - `event_log.metadata` records a **redacted** user — the `PUBLIC_USER_FIELDS`
    projection, no password hash. (The template passed the whole row; on
    `auth/login` that row carries the hash, since `check_password` needs it.)
    `event_log` is still user data — treat it like `user`.
  - Every endpoint (including the `auth/me` GET) writes an `event_log` row; the
    table grows unbounded with no pruning.
  - A valid token for a deleted user → `auth/me` yields no user. Typed
    `PublicUser | null`; the runtime outcome is most likely a 500 (the stack
    drills `user.id` out of a null `db.get`), not a 200 with a null body.
  - `password` is taken as `input.text()`, never `input.password()` — the column
    hashes on write, so an input-level hash would double-hash and break
    `check_password`. Do not "tighten" it.
  - Tokens live 24h with no refresh or revocation.
- **Identity is the consumer's lock, not this package.** Commit `xano.lock` to
  keep guids and the API URL stable across re-imports.
